title: arXiv Trending AI — 14 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ranking. Citation evidence is sparse for a one-day-old announcement batch, and no citation counts or velocity were used.

sections.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
sections.abstract: Introduces Tev-Gym, 1,170 verified long-horizon tasks across seven domains, and progress-potential reward shaping; the authors report gains on Agents’ Last Exam and transfer to Terminal-Bench.
sections.claimed_contribution: Constructs tasks from a verified latent world and uses intermediate-state progress as dense RL feedback; authors report Tev-27B matches named frontier systems at Pass@5 on ALE-CM and transfers to Terminal-Bench.
sections.unique_caveat: The study focuses on synthetic terminal environments; the hardest benchmarks retain a gap to leading frontier agents, and adding new workflows requires authoring and validating more environment components.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four configured AI category listings, an accompanying project page, and paper-hub visibility; reported evaluation spans ALE-CM and Terminal-Bench.

sections.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
sections.abstract: Uses generated reference images, a design graph, and separate verifiable and VLM-judged rewards to train code models to create editable visual artifacts with better aesthetics and content fidelity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a graph-conditioned reward design and benchmark; AesCode-8B and AesCode-32B improve visual quality over same-scale Qwen3-VL baselines with the same references by 31.1 and 22.4 percentage points.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify pixel-level geometry, complex relations, and semantic visual elements as remaining challenges.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper has an accompanying Microsoft AesCode repository and Hugging Face paper page; the technical evaluation separates correctness and visual quality.

sections.title: Visual Tokens on Demand: Visual Budgeting for Scalable and Efficient Multi-Image Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs
sections.abstract: Proposes mmVB, a query-conditioned module that assigns per-image token budgets without retraining the base model or reading inference-time attention matrices; the authors report 9× fewer visual tokens while retaining 94.4% of full-resolution accuracy over eight benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 9× fewer visual tokens, 7× fewer prefill FLOPs, and 5× faster time-to-first-token, retaining 94.4% of full-resolution accuracy across eight multi-image benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The scale predictor was trained only on natural-image QA datasets; the authors warn it may under-allocate detail in domains such as medical imaging.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Specific efficiency results and an eight-benchmark evaluation, alongside visibility on multiple paper-summary/index pages.

sections.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
sections.abstract: Combines inspectable text interaction with latent reasoning through a hybrid agent architecture and post-training methods; the authors report improvements on 11 benchmarks alongside lower token use, faster inference, and lower cost.
sections.claimed_contribution: Introduces HybridLink, HybridSFT, and HybridRL; authors report 10.4% higher performance than compared agent systems, with 35.5–54.7% fewer tokens and faster, cheaper inference.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is bounded by 11 benchmarks and three tested scales; broader task and model generalization remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in three configured AI categories and reports evaluations across 11 benchmarks and three model scales; independent attention evidence was not established.

sections.title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents
sections.abstract: Trains step-level confidence against eventual episode outcomes; authors report better calibration and selective execution on offline trajectories and in online ALFWorld experiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: Calibrates action confidence against full multi-step episode success rather than step correctness; reported online results reduce expected calibration error from 0.42 to below 0.12.
sections.unique_caveat: Experiments use Qwen2.5-7B trajectories and a live ALFWorld setting; the paper reports that identifying failure on a particular attempt is harder than predicting task-level failure.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: AI/ML cross-list and concrete offline/online evaluation signals, including AUROC and calibration error; no independent attention evidence was established.

sections.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
sections.abstract: Defines a framework for assessing physical recursive self-improvement in robots and reviews methods, safety mechanisms, and research priorities; the authors conclude that existing work does not yet meet their definition.
sections.claimed_contribution: Proposes an L0–L5 framework separating capability-level updates from meta-level learning; authors say the surveyed literature has not demonstrated Physical RSI as defined.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a framework and literature analysis, not an experimental demonstration that a robot has achieved independently verified recursive improvement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across AI, ML, and robotics and surfaced by a paper-index/summary site; it is a taxonomy and synthesis rather than an experimental demonstration.

sections.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
sections.abstract: Introduces a training-free method that audits whether agents use information faithfully at handoffs, reporting improved attribution accuracy on failed multi-agent runs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report best-or-tied step accuracy among eight strategies under a shared Jev decision interface, with a 2.2–11.1 percentage-point advantage over All-at-once.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison is bounded to failed runs and a shared Jev decision interface; broader agent setups and non-failure cases are not established by the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: AI/language cross-list and quantified comparison on 1,228 failed runs across five subsets; independent attention evidence was not established.

sections.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
sections.abstract: Formalizes agent-harness revisions as persistent changes to prompts, memory, tools, control logic, and plugins, and analyzes generalization and retention under explicit assumptions.
sections.claimed_contribution: Distinguishes harness update targets and admission mechanisms, deriving generalization and retention bounds under stated assumptions and motivating independent validation.
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantees are conditional on explicit assumptions and historical regression budgets; continued validation is needed as tasks and evaluators shift.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two configured AI-category listings and formal analysis of validation and regression; it is mainly theoretical/framework work, with no independent attention signal established.
